# @rootnative/impulse

> Declarative gesture primitives for React Native, built on
> react-native-gesture-handler. One hook per intent. Hooks return shared values
> and a gesture. Impulse starts no animation and ships no components.

Status: 0.0.0-alpha.2. Eight intents ship. A device sweep on an Android
emulator and an iOS simulator drove every intent. It proves mechanics, not
feel, so every default below is still a design intention.

Docs: https://rootnative.github.io/impulse/
Full: https://rootnative.github.io/impulse/llms-full.txt
Source: https://github.com/rootnative/impulse

## Install

Platforms: iOS and Android supported (alpha; every intent driven on a
simulator and an emulator, no physical device). Web partial: useTap,
useDoubleTap, useLongPress, useDrag verified under a mouse in a desktop
browser; usePan, useSwipe, usePinch, useRotate not verified; no automated web
test. Web needs react-dom and react-native-web. Electron, macOS, Windows: not
tested. Details: https://rootnative.github.io/impulse/installation#platforms
and https://rootnative.github.io/impulse/web

npm install @rootnative/impulse

Peers (the Expo SDK 58 band): react >=19.3.0, react-native >=0.88.0 <0.89.0,
react-native-gesture-handler >=3.3.0 <4.0.0, react-native-reanimated >=4.7.0
<4.8.0, react-native-worklets >=0.13.0 <0.14.0. An Expo SDK 57 app uses
0.0.0-alpha.1. Impulse builds gestures with the Gesture Handler builder API
(Gesture.Pan()); a Gesture Handler 3 hook gesture (usePanGesture) does not
compose with an Impulse gesture.

Render a <GestureHandlerRootView> above every component that uses a gesture.
If it is missing, gestures never fire. Gesture Handler 3 throws in development
on iOS and Android, and in Jest (wrap each render: { wrapper:
GestureHandlerRootView }). On web and in a release build, nothing warns.

## What ships

Intent hooks: useTap, useDoubleTap, useLongPress, useDrag, usePan, useSwipe,
usePinch, useRotate. Composition: useGestures. Escape hatch: useRawGesture.
The package entry re-exports GestureDetector.

NOT IMPLEMENTED, do not import: useHover, useEdgeSwipe.
They are designed only.

usePan and useDrag are not synonyms. useDrag owns a position: x and y
accumulate across gestures and bounds clamps them. usePan owns nothing: it
reports translation, velocity, and a per-frame change that you add up, and it
zeroes at every gesture.

useSwipe is a pan judged at release. directions is also the activation
criterion. An all-horizontal list gives a directional threshold, so the swipe
shares a view with a vertical scroller with no relation declared.

usePinch owns a scale that accumulates across gestures, so min and max are
the viewer's zoom range, not one gesture's. focal is the midpoint between the
fingers, and the point the zoom must happen about. A zoom about the centre of
the view slides the content out from under the fingers. It has NO activation
criteria. RNGH's pinch exposes no threshold, so only a relation separates a
pinch and a pan: useGestures([pinch, pan], { mode: 'simultaneous' }).

useRotate reports DEGREES, not the radians RNGH reports. This is the one
place Impulse changes a unit: min: -45, not -Math.PI / 4. It applies to
angle, gestureAngle, velocity and the min/max range. The angle accumulates
and does NOT wrap. A second full turn reports 720. anchor is the point the
turn happens about, the counterpart of pinch's focal. It has NO activation
criteria either, so you compose rotate and pinch as simultaneous.

Subpaths: @rootnative/impulse/{tap,double-tap,long-press,drag,pan,swipe,pinch,rotate,compose,raw,gesture-handler}

## The shape of every hook

const tap = useTap({ onTap: select })
tap.gesture    // hand to <GestureDetector>
tap.ref        // name it in another hook's alongside / blocks / deferTo
tap.isActive   // SharedValue<boolean>

useDrag adds x and y, both SharedValue<number>, both writable, both
accumulating across gestures.

## Threads — the callback name states the thread

JS thread: onTap, onDoubleTap, onLongPress, onLongPressEnd, onDragStart,
onDragEnd, onPanStart, onPanEnd, onSwipe, onSwipeEnd, onPinchStart,
onPinchEnd, onRotateStart, onRotateEnd. They are ordinary functions. Impulse
owns the scheduleOnRN boundary.

Every callback that reports an ending takes a second argument, { cancelled }:
onTap, onDoubleTap, onLongPressEnd, onDragEnd, onPanEnd, onSwipeEnd,
onPinchEnd, onRotateEnd. It fires on both endings. cancelled is true when the
system took the gesture away: a competing gesture won, the app went to the
background, or a relation handed the touch on. onSwipe fires for a commit
only and takes no second argument.

Worklets: onBegin, onUpdate, onFinalize. Mark them with 'worklet'. A plain
function there makes Impulse warn once in development, and the warning names
the hook and the callback. Without the directive, the first touch that
reaches the phase throws "Tried to synchronously call a Remote Function".
Worklets are direct gesture dependencies, so keep their identity stable. An
inline worklet rebuilds the gesture on every render. An inline JS-thread
callback doesn't.

## Composition

useGestures(members, { mode }) where mode is race | simultaneous | exclusive.
A composed result is itself a member. Precedence reads left to right.

A tap and a double tap are exclusive with the double tap FIRST, never race. A
single tap recognizes on the first release and would win every race. The
composed single tap then pays maxDelay in latency.

useGestures doesn't accept coexistence options. Put them on the members.

## Coexistence

alongside -> both recognize          (simultaneousWithExternalGesture)
blocks    -> this gesture wins       (blocksExternalGesture)
deferTo   -> the named gesture wins  (requireExternalGestureToFail)

Name another hook's .ref, not its .gesture.

TRAP: a relation target must carry a handlerTag. React Native's ScrollView has
none, and neither has Gesture Handler 3's own ScrollView, so RNGH drops the
relation SILENTLY on every platform. Use LegacyScrollView / LegacyFlatList,
from @rootnative/impulse/gesture-handler.

TRAP: a component ref needs `as unknown as GestureReference`. RNGH types the
target as a ref to a component type, and ref={} doesn't produce that type.

## Defaults

useTap: pointers 1, maxDuration 500ms, maxDistance 10pt
useDoubleTap: same, plus maxDelay 500ms (probably too generous; 250-300 is
  closer to what platforms use)
useLongPress: minDuration 500ms, maxDistance 10pt
useDrag: axis both, threshold 10pt, elastic 0, unbounded
usePan: axis both, threshold 10pt
useSwipe: directions all four, threshold 10pt, commitDistance 80pt,
  commitSpeed 800pt/s
usePinch: initial 1, unbounded, no activation criteria
useRotate: initial 0, unbounded, no activation criteria

No default has a feel result. The device sweep proved that the drag
threshold, commitDistance, and maxDelay at 500ms and 250ms work. commitSpeed
is not tested, because neither harness can make a swipe that fast.

## isActive does not mean the same thing in every hook

useTap and useDoubleTap set it at touch-down. For useTap that is a real
pressed state. For useDoubleTap it is true for every ordinary single tap on
the view too, so don't drive a pressed state from it.
useLongPress, useDrag, usePan, useSwipe, usePinch and useRotate set it at
recognition.

## Known gaps a consumer can hit

- Impulse reports a cancel, but its velocity is not a throw. The finger never
  lifted on a cancelled gesture, so a spring on velocity when cancelled is
  true flings a view that the finger never released.
- useLongPress maxDistance cancels an ACTIVE press on web, against RNGH's own
  documented contract. Hold-then-drag doesn't work there at the default.
- A missing <GestureHandlerRootView> fails silently on web and in a release
  build. Impulse adds no warning of its own.
- Web is surveyed by hand. No jsdom test pins any of it.

## Out of scope, by decision

No components. No animation vocabulary, springs or easing. No haptics policy.
useDrag returns values and no style. @rootnative/inertia-gestures has a
useDrag that returns an animatedStyle and requires @rootnative/inertia.
